definitions.explanation: To accept or pick up electronic communications or signals that have been sent. The counterpart of {送信|そうしん}する.

examples.japanese: メールを{受信|じゅしん}した。
この{部屋|へや}では{電波|でんぱ}を{受信|じゅしん}しにくい。
examples.english: It's hard to receive a signal in this room.

examples.japanese: {緊急|きんきゅう}{地震|じしん}{速報|そくほう}を{受信|じゅしん}すると、スマホから{警告音|けいこくおん}が{鳴|な}る。
examples.english: When an emergency earthquake alert is received, a warning sound goes off on the smartphone.

notes:
The counterpart of {送信|そうしん}する (to send/transmit). Used for receiving electronic communications, broadcast signals, or data. The noun form {受信|じゅしん} is also common in compound words.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- メールを{受信|じゅしん}する: to receive an email
- {電波|でんぱ}を{受信|じゅしん}する: to receive a radio signal
- {受信|じゅしん}トレイ: inbox
- {受信|じゅしん}{拒否|きょひ}: blocking reception (of calls/messages)
- {受信|じゅしん}{料|りょう}: reception fee (e.g., NHK)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {受|う}け{取|と}る: to receive — general-purpose; includes physical items
- {着信|ちゃくしん}: incoming call/message — specifically for phone calls and notifications
- {傍受|ぼうじゅ}する: to intercept — receiving communications not intended for you
